before_after_simulation.label: synthetic closed loop, 180 s, 320-550 mm sweep, starts from the observed pinned state

changes.tools/wizard/exposure.py: ROI metering with marker masking; hard/soft clipping split; dead band; headroom guard; no-op suppression; limit reporting; readback tracking; status(); stale ROI hold.
changes.tools/wizard/gui/modern_window.py: RoiHold wiring; stationary freeze input; one baseline reset per recording; logs requested/applied/readback/stats; writes exposure-status.json; ui_metrics status.

readback.capture_stderr: warning: volatile settings change rejected: volatile settings: gain camera 2: device status 3 for camera/0x27

root_causes: RGB gain no-op: the up branch assigned min(max_gain, gain+step) and recorded changes['rgb_gain'] without checking that it moved; at gain 300 every evaluation re-requested 300 (29/60 entries).

Full-frame fallback: _plate_bbox returned None whenever detection was lost (most rejected decisions), so mean came from the dark background (p50 14-45 in the log) and the loop raised exposure; RGB was driven to 20000 us / gain 300 and pinned for 58/60 entries.

Saturation measured on the full sensor included the deliberately clipped retro-reflective markers (1 % threshold), so normal marker clipping fought the dark rule with 25 % up / 20 % down steps; 17 IR direction reversals in 447 s.
Freeze bypass: emergency used full-frame p99>=250 / sat>2 %, true whenever markers were in view, so the accepted-view freeze almost never held.
Double evaluation gate (GUI 0.75 s + advisor 1.0 s) made the effective evaluation interval ~1.5 s; two-observation confirmation made changes ~3.2 s apart.

Reasons did not describe the action (RGB-only changes logged 'within target'; mean-high down logged 'saturation'; 2 entries blamed saturation at p99 214/231), and the log stored the request, not the device readback.
The capture child applies an existing exposure-control.txt at startup, so a new recording inherited the previous run's pinned 2325/20000/300 instead of the configured baseline.
exposure.jsonl is append-only across runs with no run id: 33/93 entries belong to an earlier capture, so the retained file cannot be read as one session.

tests.full_suite_failures_note: test_wizard_plate3d (2) and test_wizard_moving_replay are unrelated to exposure; plate3d.py has concurrent uncommitted edits by another agent, and moving_replay passed when rerun alone.
